name: wato_eve_labels
purpose: Vectorised map ground truth for lane/map perception on WATonomous Eve recordings, derived from Lanelet2 maps. Shared so dataset work can be distributed without duplicating conversion effort.

ego.note: same frame the BEV map head and the planner use

coordinate_frames.transform: p_ego = R(-yaw) * (p_utm - ego_utm), yaw from the frame record

patch.note: only geometry within 70 m of the ego position is kept; polylines are clipped at the patch edge, not truncated to their first point

raster_grid.note: used by masks/ and by the segmentation head; see scripts/lanelet_rasterize.py

classes.note: walkway and carpark_area are not present in these maps and get zero class weight; the six-channel head contract is unchanged

boundary.caveat: the source maps carry no paint tags (roads_around_campus.osm says left_marking/right_marking = none), so dash/solid and white/yellow are geometric inferences, not observed paint

topology.method: geometric chaining: end->start within 2 m and heading within 35 deg
topology.note: OSM Lanelet2 does not store successors; this is an approximation, so treat it as a training target, not routing ground truth

splits.rule: split by recording session, never by time: the ring road is a loop, so a time split leaks the same geometry into train and val

oldbag.source: earlier ring-road recording, frames extracted to dataset_live
oldbag.notes: the original ring-road drive used for the first fine-tune

test2.notes: only 4 frames survived the coverage filter

test5.notes: held out; different session so there is no time leakage

contents.vector_gt/vector_gt.jsonl: the vector ground truth, one JSON object per frame
contents.masks/: raster ground truth (4 supervised channels + valid), one npz per frame, regenerated by scripts/assemble_dataset.py
contents.calib/: per-source camera/LiDAR calibration npz used when the frames were extracted
contents.maps/: Lanelet2 maps the labels were derived from
contents.scripts/: the pipeline that produced all of the above
contents.metadata/frames_manifest.json: per-frame pose/coverage record from the extractor

scripts.stream_extract.py: bag -> frames: rclone HTTP-range streaming, one frame per 20 m of travel above 2 m/s; writes 6 camera JPEGs + LiDAR points + calib
scripts.lanelet_rasterize.py: Lanelet2 -> BEV raster (4 classes + valid) on the 200x200 @0.5 m grid
scripts.assemble_dataset.py: frames -> masks/manifest, applies the coverage filter (>=10%)
scripts.export_vector_gt.py: frames -> vector_gt.jsonl: lanes/boundaries/topology in ego frame
scripts.vector_targets.py: vector GT -> fixed-size training targets (K=20 points, clipped)
scripts.make_metadata.py: regenerates this file from the data

quality.note: boundaries can degenerate to 0-1 points where the 70 m patch clip cut them; centrelines never do. Training targets use the centreline, so this does not affect the vector model's targets, but a boundary-predicting head should filter these.

caveats: paint attributes (dash/solid, white/yellow) are derived from lane adjacency, not observed
divider labels come from lanelet geometry, which can sit ~10-30 cm off the painted line
topology is geometrically chained, not a routing graph
frames themselves (~2.4 MB each, 1.5 GB total) are not in this repo; only the labels are
sessions were recorded in daylight on the ring road; no night/rain coverage yet
